topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestLeadershipTransferMovesActiveSequencer`
topIssues.author: geoknee
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Confirmed flake — failed once, then passed on a rerun of the identical commit with no code change.

**Test:** `TestLeadershipTransferMovesActiveSequencer`
**File:** `op-acceptance-tests/tests/base/conductor/leadership_transfer_test.go`
**Job:** `memory-all-opn-op-reth-fusaka`

## Occurrences

| When | Job | Branch | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-09-17 11:03 UTC | [5574188](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5574188) | `gk/lagoon-span-batch-client-rules` (#22922) | **fail** — 1 of 245 acceptance tests |
| 2026-09-17 (rerun, same commit) | [5574386](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5574386) | same | pass |

Encountered while working on #22922, whose diff touches only op-node span-batch decode and the kona protocol crate and cannot reach op-conductor.

## Failure output

```
raft_logger.go:27:  WARN [09-17|11:14:43.296] heartbeat timeout reached, starting election
                         component=conductor name=sequencer chain=901 component=raft
                         last-leader-addr= last-leader-id=

raft.go:290:        ERROR[09-17|11:14:49.161] failed to transfer leadership to server
                         component=conductor name=sequencer chain=901 id=b
                         addr=127.0.0.1:36039 err="leadership transfer timeout"

    Error Trace:  /home/circleci/project/op-devstack/dsl/conductor.go:386
    Error:        Received unexpected error:
                  leadership transfer timeout
    Test:         TestLeadershipTransferMovesActiveSequencer

--- FAIL: TestLeadershipTransferMovesActiveSequencer (12.55s)
```

## Likely cause

The two log lines are ~6 seconds apart and look causally linked: raft loses its leader (`heartbeat timeout reached, starting election`, with `last-leader-addr=` and `last-leader-id=` both empty), and the explicit `TransferLeader` the test then issues times out because the cluster is mid-election with no leader to transfer *from*.

If that reading is right, this is a raft timing race rather than a product bug: the test asks for a leadership transfer without first establishing that a stable leader exists, so a heartbeat timeout landing in the wrong place fails it. The fix would be to wait for a settled leader before requesting the transfer, and/or to retry the transfer when it returns `leadership transfer timeout`, rather than to lengthen the timeout.

## How often

Rare — as far as I can measure, this is the **first recorded occurrence**:

- Walked the 300 most recent CircleCI pipelines, inspected all 37 failed `memory-all*` jobs and grepped their logs: exactly 1 hit, the one above.
- CircleCI insights for `memory-all-opn-op-reth-fusaka` on `develop`: 5 failures in 217 runs (97.7%) over 2026-08-11 → 2026-09-16, but the most-failed-tests window (100 runs) does not list this test, and the flaky-tests endpoint records a different test for this job (`TestInteropFilter_IngressRejectsInvalid`).
- No pre-existing issue matches the test name.

Filing it anyway so the next occurrence lands somewhere rather than being rediscovered.

## Possibly related

`TestSequencerFailover_DisasterRecovery_OverrideLeader` — 1/62 failures in `go-tests` per CircleCI insights. Different test, same conductor-leadership area, and plausibly the same underlying raft-timing sensitivity. Worth checking together if anyone picks this up.

topIssues.title: kona-sp1: revm-precompile 42 pulls sha2 0.11, which has no SP1 patch
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Situation

revm-precompile 42 (pulled in by reth v2.5.0, #22495) depends on `sha2 = "0.11"`. The SP1 guest workspace accelerates SHA-256 by patching `sha2` with [sp1-patches/RustCrypto-hashes](https://github.com/sp1-patches/RustCrypto-hashes), and a `[patch.crates-io]` entry only replaces the version it names: the guest patches [`sha2 0.10.9`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2191ce5dd2569534fb3016f7a931eabc78cc6f8c/rust/kona/sp1/programs/Cargo.toml#L137). sp1-patches has no `patch-sha2-0.11.*` tag (only mirrors of the upstream `sha2-v0.11.0-*` tags), and Succinct's own zkevm still pins patched 0.10.9.

So the guest now carries two `sha2` crates: patched 0.10.9 (alloy, kona) and vanilla 0.11.0, whose only dependent is revm-precompile. Two consensus paths hash through the vanilla copy inside the zkVM: the SHA-256 precompile (0x02) and the KZG point-evaluation versioned-hash check. Correctness is unaffected; those hashes run as plain RISC-V cycles instead of the SHA-256 syscalls, i.e. a proving-cost regression. `check-sp1-guest-precompile-patches` caught it.

## Workaround in #22495

revm 42 routes both hashes through its pluggable `Crypto` trait, so kona's `CustomCrypto` now [implements `sha256`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2191ce5dd2569534fb3016f7a931eabc78cc6f8c/rust/kona/sp1/crates/client/src/precompiles/custom.rs#L24) with the client crate's own `sha2`, which is the patched 0.10 line in the guest. The vanilla 0.11 stays compiled in as dead code (`DefaultCrypto`), so the CI check gained an [exemption](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2191ce5dd2569534fb3016f7a931eabc78cc6f8c/rust/justfile#L298-L318): an unpatched `sha2` is tolerated only while revm-precompile is its sole dependent.

Residual risk: the guard checks the dependency graph, not call sites. A future revm-precompile that hashes with `sha2` directly instead of through `Crypto` would regress silently.

## Follow-up

1. **SP1 (Succinct):** publish a `patch-sha2-0.11.0-sp1-6.x` tag in sp1-patches/RustCrypto-hashes. revm-precompile ≥ 42 (revm 42, reth ≥ v2.5.0) requires sha2 0.11, so every SP1 program executing a current revm is affected, not only kona.
2. **Here, once the tag exists:** add `sha2 0.11` to the guest's `[patch.crates-io]`, delete the `CustomCrypto::sha256` override and the check exemption, and restore the strict "every sha2 resolves from sp1-patches" invariant.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.1*

topIssues.title: flake: reth-optimism-node integration test peers_negotiate_eth_69 SIGSEGVs on teardown
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Filed on behalf of @ajsutton.

## Test

`reth-optimism-node::it p2p_version::peers_negotiate_eth_69` — `rust/op-reth/crates/node/tests/it/p2p_version.rs`

## CI evidence

- Job: https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/126050/workflows/6f052c6e-19a6-47dc-9a51-6e6f03473058/jobs/5100649
- Workflow: `rust-ci-gate-short` / `op-reth-integration-tests`
- Triggered on merge-queue branch for PR #20963

## Symptom

The test's assertions all pass — nextest reports:

```
test p2p_version::peers_negotiate_eth_69 ... ok
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 7 filtered out; finished in 5.13s
(test aborted with signal 11: SIGSEGV)
```

The crash is during process teardown after the test body returns Ok. Nextest marks the run as failed because the binary exited with a signal, killing the merge-queue check.

## Suspected area

The test spins up two op-reth nodes via `reth_optimism_node::utils::setup(2)` and queries the admin RPC to confirm peers negotiate eth/69. The body completes cleanly; the SIGSEGV happens as the tokio runtime / p2p stack / native networking resources are dropped at process exit.

## Reported occurrences

This flake has been observed on multiple recent runs (per @ajsutton). No prior `C-flake` issue existed for this test.

## Next step

Investigation underway via op-claude flake-fixer agent.

topPRs.title: Silhouette: private interoperable chains (v1, attested)
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## Silhouette: private interoperable chains (v1, attested) A silhouette chain is a private L2 that participates in an ordinary interop dependency set. Its transactions stay private. L1 carries a signed proof envelope describing the chain's public outline and a standard derivation carrier with user transactions removed. v1 is explicitly operator-attested: the trusted submitter's L1 signature authenticates the claimed state. The wire reserves a proof slot for a future proven mode, but this PR contains no ZK toolchain or L1 settlement path. ### Architecture - **No `op-node` changes.** The final PR diff under `op-node/` is empty. - **No custom submitter.** The normal `op-batcher` loads real private blocks, receipts and output roots and retains its normal channel, reorg, txmgr and retry lifecycle. A terminal encoder emits the silhouette proof envelope followed by standard carrier frames for the same block cadence with user transactions removed. - **Normal inbox and stock portal.** Both envelope and carrier go to the rollup's normal batch inbox. Deposits remain enabled and are stock-derived; there is no gated portal contract. - **Stock derivation.** A stock verifier `op-node` ignores the `KCPB` proof blob as an unknown derivation format, consumes the following standard carrier frames, and runs the ordinary Holocene/interop rewind and deposits-only replacement path. - **One verifier-only supernode role.** Silhouette chains cannot be sequenced by a supernode virtual node. Private sequencing is performed by a LightCL op-node backed by the private EL. - **Standalone magic EL.** `op-silhouette-el` is an in-memory Engine/eth RPC service. It watches the authenticated proof stream independently, maps stock carrier attributes to proof-committed block hashes and roots, and delegates a stock deposits-only replacement build to the private EL when interop invalidates a proven block. - **Normal interop semantics.** The supernode's stock judge validates the private chain's declared imports against independently derived public-chain messages. Invalid blocks are replaced and transitive invalidation propagates across chains. ### What is posted to L1 Each normal batcher submission contains: 1. `KCPB` envelope magic, wire version, public-values length/data, and proof length/data (empty in attested mode). 2. Batch commitments: previous/new output root, L1 head hash, rollup-config hash, dependency-set hash, export-policy hash, and the block list. 3. Per block: number, timestamp, real block hash, state root, message-passer storage root, exported logs, imported messages, L1-origin hash/number, and sequence number. 4. Per exported log: real block log index, log hash, and optional preimage (empty under the default all-hashes policy). 5. Per imported message: origin, source block/log index/timestamp/chain ID, and payload hash. 6. Standard compressed derivation channel/frame data carrying each block's parent, epoch, timestamp, stock deposits/L1-info transaction, and an empty user-transaction list. It does **not** publish private user transaction bytes or hashes, senders, calldata, receipts, contract state, or full log contents. The ordinary L1 blob transaction still exposes its sender, destination inbox, nonce, fees, commitments and inclusion block. ### Images Build these three branch-specific targets: ```sh docker buildx bake op-batcher op-supernode op-silhouette-el ``` | Image | Difference from a normal interop deployment | |---|---| | `op-batcher` | Enables the terminal silhouette proof + stripped-carrier encoding. | | `op-supernode` | Loads the silhouette verifier manifest and proof observer. It remains verifier-only. | | `op-silhouette-el` | New in-memory proof-backed Engine/eth service used as P's verifier EL. | The standalone `op-node`, L1/L2 execution clients, and portal contracts are stock. There is no `proofbatch-submitter` image. ### Minimal configuration delta Private producer: ```sh op-batcher --data-availability-type blobs --silhouette \ --max-pending-tx 1 --target-num-frames 6 \ --silhouette.inbox $NORMAL_BATCH_INBOX --silhouette.wire-version 4 \ --silhouette.rollup-config-hash $ROLLUP_HASH \ --silhouette.dependency-set-hash $DEPSET_HASH ``` The producer is otherwise a normal LightCL sequencer + private EL. It uses the stock `OptimismPortal`; the silhouette inbox must equal the normal rollup batch inbox. Magic EL: ```sh op-silhouette-el --l1 $L1_RPC --l1.beacon $L1_BEACON \ --supernode $SUPERNODE_RPC --rollup-config rollup-p.json \ --verifier-config verifier-p.json \ --replacement-engine $PRIVATE_ENGINE_AUTH_RPC \ --replacement-engine.jwt-secret jwt.txt --rpc.addr 0.0.0.0 --rpc.port 9545 ``` Verifier supernode: ```sh op-supernode --silhouette manifest.json \ --vn.

.l2 http://op-silhouette-el:9545 \ --vn.

.interop.dependency-set depset.json ``` The `op-node` VN has no silhouette/private flag: its only unusual input is that its configured EL endpoint speaks the proof-backed Engine API. The manifest names P's verifier config; A is absent and remains an ordinary chain. The verifier config binds L1 chain ID, trusted submitter, normal inbox, rollup/dependency-set hashes, `proofType: "attested"`, `wireVersion: 4`, and the anchor. ### Local network and smoke tests ```sh go run ./op-up --silhouette # funded transactional RPCs: A http://127.0.0.1:8545, B http://127.0.0.1:8546 go run ./op-up smoke-interop all go run ./op-up smoke-interop invalid-message --direction both --reorg-timeout 5m go run ./op-up smoke-interop chained-invalid-message --require-cascade --reorg-timeout 5m # comparison topology go run ./op-up --interop ``` Observed locally on this revision: - silhouette `smoke-interop all`: PASS; - bidirectional invalid A→B and B→A: both replaced and both chains resumed; - strict chained invalidation: invalid P block, direct dependent, and descendant dependent all reorged while the independent control remained; - normal sysgo bidirectional invalid smoke: same replacement/resume semantics (lower latency because it does not wait for the proof-batch cadence); - focused `TestSilhouetteImportThatIsFalseIsReplaced`: PASS; - `op-batcher`, all `op-supernode`, sysgo/presets, smoke utility, and `op-up` unit suites: PASS. The serialized full silhouette acceptance package still has one known timeout in `TestSilhouetteCrossChainPinsThenAdvances`; the replacement regression and proof-slot refusal tests pass independently. ### Diff size Against the PR base: approximately **24.3k insertions / 1.45k deletions across 267 files**. Much of the file count is the existing cross-language fixture corpus. The architecture rewrite in the latest commit is **3,487 insertions / 7,004 deletions**: it deletes the custom submitter, sequencing-side silhouette role, custom portal, and op-node hook in favor of the stock paths above. Operational details and the exact trust statement live in `op-supernode/silhouette/docs/RUNNING-V1.md` and `TRUST-MODEL.md`.

topPRs.title: interop: suspend atomic demo router execution
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #22840. The atomic demo now supports nested cross-chain callbacks while retaining one live OP EVM transaction per chain. A on chain A calls B on chain B; B uses the same facade/router mechanism to call a distinct C on chain A; C sees A's pending state and can call back into the still-running B. The callback executes inside each chain's original transaction, preserving pending storage, transient storage, origin, gas ancestry and rollback. Each included chain receives one final replay after callback/result tapes and access lists are materialized; divergence rejects the candidate without discovery restarts or padding.

Canonical callback dispatch runs through ordinary router bytecode. Gas remains local to each chain: top-level application calls have fixed budgets, while callbacks receive half the remaining gas at their dispatch point. Caller context is restored on return, scheduling depth is capped at 32, and the bundle-wide call limit still applies. Failed callback hints force application rollback even if caught. ERC-4337 uses the existing EntryPoint and demo paymaster for normal on-chain gas settlement; it does not reimburse off-chain discovery or prove that a builder honestly attempted success. Existing Go and Kona cycle algorithms remain unchanged.

The Go/devstack bridge uses pinned candidate-prefix state and exact signed envelopes. This is a **demo node integration**; production payload-service admission/publication and a single-signature wallet flow remain out of scope. ETH forwarding, STATICCALL facades and committing after a caught remote failure remain unsupported. The original Go discovery path remains available for root-driven calls; nested dispatch is connected to the suspended builder.

Validation passed: all 18 contracts PR checks; full developer contract suite (2,290 passed, 183 skipped) and optimized suite (2,350 passed, 159 skipped); all 40 Rust builder tests with artifact-dependent tests enabled, including optimized bytecode; full Rust workspace lint/rustdoc and Go lint; Go bridge/message/filter/verifier tests; and Go/Kona nested-cycle regressions. All four real-node suspended/nested ERC-4337 success/revert cases pass, including exact receipt gas/log parity and sponsor settlement. Contract checks used the configured Foundry remappings plus explicit Solady/OpenZeppelin mappings with automatic remapping disabled to avoid the local duplicate `src/src` import issue.

Solidity, Rust lifecycle/application-effect and Go reviews are complete; all findings were fixed, none dismissed. Shared node fixtures are included by the normal contracts artifact build. #22840's branch remains unchanged.

CI on `ac7332b5d4af30420badf96e670243ec59df941d` is complete but not green: title/dependency checks and five Wiz scanners passed; Wiz SAST was skipped. The x86 multicannon package built, then [artifact attestation failed because the fork workflow lacks `id-token` permission](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/actions/runs/34524915489/job/103031802906), reproducing the previous head's permission failure. The other seven package jobs were canceled by fail-fast; image/smoke jobs were skipped. Full upstream CI for this fork still requires human authorization.

topPRs.title: kona-node,op-reth,op-batcher: multi-blocks PoC (up to max_multi_blocks blocks per block time)
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
**Draft / PoC, work in progress — CI feedback only for now.**

Multi-blocks: keep `block_time`, allow the sequencer to build up to `max_multi_blocks` L2 blocks sharing one timestamp after a feature timestamp `multi_block_time` (≥ Karst, not a hardfork). Sealing policy is the builder's choice; consensus only bounds the group size. Chain consistency is parent-hash linkage.

Scope of the PoC: kona-node (sequencer + derivation), op-reth (EL), op-batcher (span batch v2), op-devstack + acceptance tests on a kona-node/op-reth-only devnet. op-node keeps rejecting span batch v2; interop, proofs, flashblocks and registry support are out of scope.

Landed so far (one commit per workstream):
- op-reth: `ts == parent.ts` accepted iff siblings are allowed at `ts`; builder seal policy flags; `engine_awaitPayloadReadyV1`
- kona: `multi_block_time`/`max_multi_blocks` config; `BatchType::SpanV2` = Delta span + `same_ts_bits` (bit 0 = sibling of the span's parent, so groups may straddle spans/channels)
- Go: rollup/deploy config, span batch v2 codec + `SpanChannelOut` switch, devstack options and DSL helpers, shared golden vectors

Still to come: kona derivation validity, kona sequencer slot loop, acceptance tests.

Judgement calls worth a look:
- the `min-build-time` policy only seals a payload that holds ≥ 1 user tx, so an idle sequencer still makes one block per block time
- straddling groups across span batches/channels is allowed (bit 0), instead of forcing the batcher to keep groups atomic across L1-driven channel closes
- `siblings_allowed` is false at *every* configured fork activation timestamp, which keeps the timestamp-only `is_first_<fork>_block` predicates correct for forks scheduled after activation

topPRs.title: interop: atomic demo
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
This atomic demo lets an application call a remote contract through its normal ABI, use the returned value in subsequent calls, and roll back when the remote call or its own final check fails. CREATE2 facades provide predictable local addresses. Serial discovery constructs transactions across N chains using the existing CrossL2Inbox, access-list requirements, and cycle rules; no existing protocol contract or execution-client rule changes.

The sponsored path uses signed ERC-4337 UserOperations, the preinstalled EntryPoint, CREATE2 smart accounts, and an opt-in paymaster. Both successful and reverting application calls consume sponsored gas without requiring ETH in the smart accounts. EntryPoint catches application reverts, so its outer receipt succeeds while the UserOperation event reports failure. The builder bounds discovery, performs one final canonical replay per included chain, checks results and message commitments, and returns the exact verified UserOperations and outer calldata/fee parameters.

Failed result hints force rollback but cannot prove that a user caused the failure. Account owners explicitly authorize sponsorship spending; there is no user billing for discarded simulations, deliberate gas burning, or public builder admission service. Discovery still restarts transactions and uses local signers for intermediate operations. Nested callbacks, ETH/view facades, interactive signed intents, SDM refund reconciliation, and a production adapter for the complete candidate block environment remain outside this prototype. In particular, the RPC adapter retains the parent's base fee and cannot guarantee gas-price-sensitive execution against a changed next-block environment. See `op-test-sequencer/atomic/DESIGN.md` for these boundaries.

Capability regression coverage and the demo are separate commits. Go and contract/security reviews cover the sponsored extension; the fee mismatch found during review is fixed with EVM/RPC regressions and pinned submission fees. A gas-trace regression also checks identical gas supplied and consumed at the application and both proxy calls between final discovery and replay, after fixing the discovery adapter's cold inbox-address surcharge. The original capability changes also received Rust and CI reviews. No review findings were dismissed.

Local validation passes for all 17 contract PR checks, the tagged EVM suite, affected Go verification packages, Go lint/module checks, and both sponsored real op-reth/supernode scenarios. The node tests verify application rollback, UserOperation success/failure, the exact paymaster deposit debit, and unfunded smart accounts. The full optimized contract suite passes with 2,335 tests and 159 skips; the final developer-mode suite passes with 2,275 tests and 183 skips. An earlier developer run was invalidated by concurrent artifact-cache replacement; the sequential rerun above is clean. The original raw node scenarios, ten native Kona cycle tests, and CI routing scenarios also passed.

Full Kona/challenger execution remains blocked at setup by missing prestate artifacts; workspace Rust clippy is blocked by missing m4 in an unrelated native dependency, and local CircleCI schema/process validation is unavailable because its CLI is absent. Native cycle tests do not substitute for full proof execution. Main upstream CI requires human authorization under the repository's fork policy.

On the current commit, GitHub dependency, title, and all Wiz checks pass. The image workflow fails at [APK provenance attestation](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/actions/runs/34422616906/job/102701496534) with `missing "id-token" permission`, the same restricted-fork failure seen on the prior head; the other image builds are canceled and downstream image/smoke jobs are skipped. This draft is not CI-green.

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: throttle ERC20 and ETH withdrawals
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds development-gated withdrawal throttling for whitelisted ERC20s and ETH using percentage-based token buckets.

- Supports `L1StandardBridge`, `OptimismPortal2`, and shared `ETHLockbox` custody.
- Uses live escrow balances, lazy exact fractional refill, and revert-on-exhaustion.
- Adds owner configuration/refresh APIs and monitoring events.
- Configures throttles through OPCM instructions behind `WITHDRAWAL_THROTTLE`.
- Centralizes accounting in a reusable two-slot packed `WithdrawalThrottle.State`.
- Conservatively saturates capacities above `uint128.max`.

Cold-path benchmarks measure throttle overhead at approximately 17.3k gas for ERC20 finalization and 14.9k gas for ETH finalization.

## Testing

Added coverage for refill precision, overflow boundaries, reconfiguration, live-stock changes, shared-lockbox behavior, OPCM configuration, storage writes, and cold-path gas benchmarks.
